'''Santosh Shivaji Lad''' (born 27 February 1975) is an Indian politician from [[Karnataka]] <ins>and a member of the [[Indian National Congress]]</ins>. He has been elected to the Karnataka Legislative Assembly four times, first from Sandur in 2004 and subsequently from Kalaghatgi in 2008, 2013 and 2023. He currently serves as the Cabinet Minister for Labour and Employment<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rao |first=Ananya |date=2026-06-04 |title=Karnataka Cabinet Ministers – DK Shivakumar Government (2026) |url=https://www.karnataka.com/govt/cabinet-ministers/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |language=en-US}}</ref> in [[Government of Karnataka]], and is a member of [[Karnataka Legislative Assembly]] representing [[Kalghatgi Assembly constituency|Kalaghatgi-Alnavar]] constituency in the Dharwad district of [[Karnataka]] state.<ref>{{cite news |title=State govt focused on welfare of labourers: Minister Santosh Lad |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hubballi/state-govt-focused-on-welfare-of-labourers-minister-santosh-lad/articleshow/100636471.cms |access-date=15 May 2025 |work=The Times of India |date=31 May 2023}}</ref>

Lad has served as a minister in successive [[Government of Karnataka|Karnataka government]]. He served as Minister of State for Information and Infrastructure Development in the [[First Siddaramaiah ministry|Siddaramaiah ministry]] from 2013, resigned from the ministry in November 2013 following allegations concerning illegal mining involving his company, and returned to the state cabinet in 2016 as Labour Minister, later also holding the Skill Development portfolio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=T. N. M. |date=2016-06-19 |title=Karnataka cabinet reshuffle: Siddaramaiah drops 14 ministers, inducts 13 |url=https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/karnataka-cabinet-reshuffle-siddaramaiah-drops-14-ministers-inducts-13-45119 |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=The News Minute |language=en}}</ref>

He was re-elected from Kalaghatgi in 2023 and appointed Labour Minister in the second Siddaramaiah ministry. He subsequently continued in the Labour portfolio after the 2026 reconstitution of the Karnataka cabinet, where the Karnataka Legislative Assembly lists him as Minister for Labour and Employment.<ref name="current">{{Cite web |last=Rao |first=Ananya |date=2026-06-04 |title=Karnataka Cabinet Ministers – DK Shivakumar Government (2026) |url=https://www.karnataka.com/govt/cabinet-ministers/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |language=en-US}}</ref>[[File:Santosh Lad with Actors.jpg|thumb|Santosh Lad with South Indian Actors]]

== Early life and education ==
Santosh Lad, son of Shailaja and Lt. Shivaji Lad, was born on 27 February 1975 in [[Sanduru|Sandur]] taluk of Karnataka's [[Bellary district]]. He has one elder sister. Lad completed a Bachelor of Commerce degree from SESS College, Sandur, in 1997, according to his election affidavit.

Lad's family has been associated with business interests in Sandur and the Ballari region. His professional occupation was listed as business/entrepreneur in his 2023 election affidavit.<ref name="affidavit">{{Cite web |title=Santosh S Lad(Indian National Congress(INC)):Constituency- KALAGHATGI(DHARWAD) - Affidavit Information of Candidate: |url=https://myneta.info/Karnataka2023/candidate.php?candidate_id=7428 |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=myneta.info}}</ref>

==Political career==

=== Early political career ===
According to Lad's published biography, he began his political career through the Sandur municipal council in 2002.

He contested the 2004 Karnataka Legislative Assembly election from the Sandur constituency as a candidate of the [[Janata Dal (Secular)]]. He defeated Congress candidate V. Y. Ghorpade, receiving 65,600 votes against Ghorpade's 30,022, a margin of 35,578 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sandur, Vidhan Sabha 2004 — IndiaVotes |url=https://www.indiavotes.com/vidhan-sabha/karnataka/2004/sandur/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=www.indiavotes.com |language=en}}</ref>

Lad subsequently joined the [[Indian National Congress]] in 2007.

=== Kalaghatgi ===
Following the 2008 delimitation of Karnataka's constituencies, Lad contested the Kalaghatgi Assembly constituency on a Congress ticket. He defeated BJP candidate C. M. Nimbannavar by 11,642 votes, receiving 49,733 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kalghatgi, Vidhan Sabha 2008 — IndiaVotes |url=https://www.indiavotes.com/vidhan-sabha/karnataka/2008/kalghatgi/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=www.indiavotes.com |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2013 Karnataka Legislative Assembly election, Lad was re-elected from Kalaghatgi. He received 76,802 votes, defeating his nearest rival by more than 45,000 votes.<ref name="2013results">{{Cite web |title=Kalghatgi, Vidhan Sabha 2013 — IndiaVotes |url=https://www.indiavotes.com/vidhan-sabha/karnataka/2013/kalghatgi/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=www.indiavotes.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, Lad contested Kalaghatgi again but was defeated by BJP candidate C. M. Nimbannavar. Nimbannavar received 83,267 votes compared with Lad's 57,270, a margin of 25,997 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kalghatgi, Vidhan Sabha 2018 — IndiaVotes |url=https://www.indiavotes.com/vidhan-sabha/karnataka/2018/kalghatgi/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=www.indiavotes.com |language=en}}</ref>

Lad returned to the Assembly in the 2023 Karnataka election. He won Kalaghatgi with 85,761 votes, defeating BJP candidate Nagaraj Chebbi, who received 71,404 votes. The margin was 14,357 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kalghatgi Assembly Karnataka Election 2023 Results Live: Kalghatgi constituency Results, Winner list and vote share |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/elections/karnataka-assembly-election/kalghatgi-1067 |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

=== Ministerial career ===

==== Information and Infrastructure Development ====
In 2013, Lad was appointed as Minister of State for Information and Infrastructure Development in the Congress government headed by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. <ref>{{Cite web |last=PTI |date=2013-05-18 |title=Siddaramaiah expands Cabinet, 28 Ministers sworn in |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/karnataka/2013/May/18/siddaramaiah-expands-cabinet-28-ministers-sworn-in-478407.html |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

As minister in charge of Dharwad district, Lad was involved in reviewing district-level development and administrative issues.

==== 2013 resignation ====
In November 2013, Lad resigned from the Karnataka cabinet following allegations relating to illegal mining involving V. S. Lad & Sons, a company associated with his family. Contemporary reports stated that the company had been accused of illegal extraction and supply/export of iron ore. Lad said he resigned to avoid embarrassment to the Congress government and described his decision as a moral one.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-11-22 |title=Santosh Lad resigns |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/santosh-lad-resigns/article5380247.ece |access-date=2026-08-27 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

The resignation followed scrutiny of mining activity in the Ballari region and allegations concerning the classification of the company's mining lease. Reporting at the time also noted that the Karnataka Lokayukta had raised allegations concerning the company's mining activities.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Karnataka minister Santosh Lad resigns over illegal mining charge |url=https://www.ndtv.com/south/karnataka-minister-santosh-lad-resigns-over-illegal-mining-charge-542083 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519070340/https://www.ndtv.com/south/karnataka-minister-santosh-lad-resigns-over-illegal-mining-charge-542083 |archive-date=2025-05-19 |access-date=2026-10-07 |work=www.ndtv.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== Labour and Skill Development, 2016–2018 ====
Lad returned to the Karnataka cabinet in June 2016 as Labour Minister during a cabinet reshuffle under Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.<ref name="2016return">{{cite news |date=19 June 2016 |title=Ministry reshuffle: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah sacks 14, inducts 13 |work=The Financial Express}}</ref>
[[File:Santosh Lad swearing ceremony as Minister of Labour, Government of Karnataka.png|alt=Santosh Lad oath taking as Labour Minister|thumb|258x258px|Santosh Lad Swearing in as Labour Minister]]
In 2017, he was given the additional charge of Skill Development.

As Labour Minister, Lad publicly supported women's participation in night-shift employment and opposed recommendations that women should be restricted from night work because of domestic responsibilities.<ref name="nightwork">{{cite news |date=20 April 2017 |title=Karnataka's minister Santosh Lad backs women's right to work on night shifts |work=The Economic Times}}</ref>

==== Return to government in 2023 ====
Lad was re-elected from Kalaghatgi in the 2023 Karnataka Assembly election and was inducted into Siddaramaiah's cabinet on 27 May 2023 as Minister for Labour.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-01 |title=Karnataka cabinet list 2023: Full list of ministers and their portfolios |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/karnataka-ministers-list-siddaramaiah-dk-shivakumar-portfolio-full-list-karnataka-ministers-2023/3088005/ |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=The Financial Express |language=en}}</ref>

He was also appointed minister in charge of Dharwad district in June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Express News |date=2023-06-10 |title=Karnataka district in-charge ministers: DK Shivakumar gets Bengaluru, Laxmi Hebbalkar Udupi |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/karnataka/2023/Jun/10/karnatakadistrict-in-charge-ministers-dk-shivakumargets-bengaluru-laxmi-hebbalkar-udupi-2583618.html |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

==== Labour and Employment, 2026-present ====
Lad is Inducted as Labour and Employment Minister of DK Shivakumar's Cabinet after reconstitution of Karnataka in 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-08-03 |title=Full list of new Karnataka Cabinet: Congress names 20 ministers, omits senior leaders |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/full-list-of-new-karnataka-cabinet-congress-names-20-ministers-omits-senior-leaders/articleshow/132826794.cms |access-date=2026-08-27 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shivam |date=2026-08-04 |title=Karnataka Cabinet Expansion 2026: 19 Ministers Inducted into CM D K Shivakumar’s Cabinet |url=https://currentaffairs.adda247.com/karnataka-cabinet-expansion-2026-19-ministers-inducted-into-cm-d-k-shivakumars-cabinet/ |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=Adda247 |language=en-IN}}</ref>

He is also entrusted with responsibility of overseeing Dharwad District as In charge Minister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rao |first=Ananya |date=2023-06-10 |title=District In-charge Ministers of Karnataka 2026 – Full List |url=https://www.karnataka.com/govt/district-in-charge-ministers/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-08-14 |title=Karnataka District In-Charge Ministers List 2026: 31 districts get new ministers; check full list |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/karnataka-district-in-charge-ministers-list-2026-31-districts-get-new-ministers-check-full-list/articleshow/133247415.cms |access-date=2026-08-31 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

== Rescue and relief operations ==
[[File:Kedarnath Floods.jpg|alt=Santosh Lad in Kedarnath |thumb|Santosh Lad in Uttarakhand rescue operation]]

=== 2013 Uttarakhand floods ===
During the 2013 Uttarakhand floods, Lad was assigned responsibility for coordinating rescue and relief operations involving stranded Kannadigas. Reporting from the disaster area described Lad and a team of officials, doctors and nurses providing food, water, medicines and evacuation assistance to stranded pilgrims.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-08-07 |title=Santosh Lad finds KIMS 'ravaged' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hubballi/Santosh-Lad-finds-KIMS-ravaged/articleshow/21661654.cms |access-date=2026-08-31 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

The New Indian Express reported that the team had helped evacuate more than 1,000 pilgrims from Karnataka during the operation.<ref name="uttarakhand2">{{cite news |date=29 June 2013 |title=The 'Lad' of the land |work=The New Indian Express}}</ref>

=== 2023 Odisha train accident ===
[[File:Wayanad landslide.jpg|alt=Wayanad Rescue Operation|thumb|Santosh Lad in Wayanad Landslide Rescue Operation]]
Following the Balasore train accident in Odisha in June 2023, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah appointed Lad to coordinate rescue and assistance for Kannadigas affected by the disaster. He was directed to travel to the site and assist injured people from Karnataka.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalappa |first=Bansy |date=2023-06-09 |title=There was so much pain and death, Karnataka Minister Santosh Lad on return from Odisha |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/karnataka/2023/Jun/09/there-was-so-much-pain-and-deathkarnataka-minister-santosh-lad-on-return-from-odisha-2583287.html |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thadhagath |first=Pathi Venkata |date=2023-06-03 |title=Odisha Train Accident: Karnataka minister Santosh lad to monitor rescue operations of Kannadigas |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/bengaluru-news/odisha-train-accident-karnataka-minister-santosh-lad-to-monitor-rescue-operations-of-kannadigas-101685777514332.html |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2024 Wayanad landslides ===
In August 2024, the Karnataka government deputed Lad to assist rescue and relief operations in Wayanad, Kerala, following devastating landslides. He camped in the affected area and coordinated with the Kerala government and Karnataka officials concerning people from Karnataka who were stranded or affected.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Express News |date=2024-08-01 |title=Karnataka government deploys Labour Minister Santosh for relief work in Wayanad |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/karnataka/2024/Aug/01/karnataka-government-deploys-labour-minister-santosh-for-relief-work-in-wayanad |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2025 Pahalgam Rescue Operation ===
At the time of Pahalgam terror attack April 2025, Santosh Lad was instructed to reach Kashmir and rescue people of Karnataka over three intense days, he coordinated the safe return of 177 Kannadigas from different parts of Kashmir.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-04-23 |title=Pahalgam terror attack: Karnataka CM rushes minister to Kashmir to ensure safe return of Kannadigas |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/pahalgam-terror-attack-karnataka-cm-rushes-minister-to-kashmir-to-ensure-safe-return-of-kannadigas/articleshow/120537557.cms |access-date=2026-08-26 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-04-25 |title=Pahalgam terror attack: Karnataka government brings back 175 tourists from Kashmir |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/karnataka-government-brings-back-175-tourists-stranded-in-kashmir/article69486500.ece |access-date=2026-08-31 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

== Labour minister ==
Lad's second period as Labour Minister has been marked by measures concerning gig workers, unorganized workers, minimum wages and women's workplace rights.

=== Gig workers ===
In July 2023, the Karnataka government announced a free life and accident insurance cover of ₹4 lakh for gig workers, consisting of ₹2 lakh each for life and accidental insurance. Lad said the initiative followed representations from gig-worker organizations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karnataka Govt Announces Rs 4 Lakh Insurance Cover For Gig Workers |url=https://www.bwpeople.in/article/karnataka-govt-announces-rs-4-lakh-insurance-cover-for-gig-workers-491026 |access-date=2026-08-31 |website=BW People |language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Karnataka Labour Minister Santosh Lad with gig workers and representatives of platform-based worker organisations..jpg|alt=Governor of Karnataka with Santosh Lad and Gig Workers|thumb|Santosh Lad with Gig Workers representing workers organizations.]]
The Labour Department subsequently notified the health and insurance cover for gig workers, Lad said the department would develop a portal through which gig workers could apply for the scheme.

In 2025, the Karnataka Legislative Assembly passed the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025. The legislation created a framework for registration of gig workers and aggregators, a welfare board and welfare fund, social-security obligations, occupational health and safety provisions, and dispute-resolution mechanisms.<ref name="gigact">{{Cite web |title=Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 {{!}} Digital Labour Platform Tracker |url=https://digitallabour.ilo.org/legislation/karnataka-platform-based-gig-workers-social-security-and-welfare-act-2025 |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=digitallabour.ilo.org}}</ref>

The Act applies to platform-based services including ride sharing, food and grocery delivery, logistics, e-marketplace services, healthcare, travel and hospitality, and content and media services. The legislation allows a welfare fee to be levied on aggregators, with the rate to be determined under the statutory framework.

=== Minimum wages ===
In May 2026, the Karnataka government revised minimum wages by approximately 60 percent across 81 scheduled sectors. Under the revised structure, the minimum monthly wage for unskilled workers in the Greater Bengaluru area was reported at ₹23,376, while highly skilled workers were entitled to ₹31,114. Rates elsewhere in Karnataka ranged between ₹19,300 and ₹21,251 depending on location and category.<ref name="wages">{{cite news |date=24 May 2026 |title=Karnataka hikes minimum wages in 81 sectors by 60% |work=The New Indian Express}}</ref>

Lad described the revision as a long-standing demand of the labour community and said the revised framework was intended to provide greater economic security to workers in the unorganized and specified sectors.<ref name="wages" />

=== Menstrual leave policy ===
In October 2025, the Karnataka cabinet approved a policy providing women employees with one paid menstrual-leave day per month, amounting to up to 12 days annually<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-14 |title=Karnataka becomes first India state to offer menstrual leave to all working women |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c78zg4810jro |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> Lad described the measure as a progressive labour policy and said it was intended to support women's health and participation in the workforce.

The policy was subsequently implemented through government orders. In December 2025, Karnataka extended the paid menstrual-leave benefit to women government employees, including contractual workers.

=== Welfare of unorganized workers ===
The Labour Department under Lad has also pursued measures aimed at extending social-security coverage to workers outside conventional organized employment. In 2024, the state introduced the Ambedkar Karmikara Sahaya Hasta Yojane for additional categories of unorganized workers, with benefits including insurance and other forms of assistance.<ref name="ambedkar">{{cite news |date=19 August 2024 |title=Santosh Lad succours Ambedkar social benefit to the unorganized sector |work=Bangalore Mail}}</ref>

In 2025, Lad proposed a ₹1-per-litre fuel cess to create a dedicated healthcare fund for unorganized workers. He said such a mechanism could generate substantial resources for worker healthcare and support a proposed health-card system.<ref name="fuelcess">{{cite news |date=11 October 2025 |title=Karnataka Labour Minister seeks Rs 1 fuel cess to fund healthcare of unorganised workers |work=The New Indian Express}}</ref>

=== Cinema and cultural workers ===
In July 2024, the Karnataka Legislative Assembly passed the Karnataka Cine and Cultural Activists (Welfare) Bill, providing for a welfare framework for workers in the cinema and cultural sector. The legislation included a proposed 2 percent cess on movie tickets and OTT subscriptions and provided for a welfare board.<ref name="cine">{{cite news |date=24 July 2024 |title=Karnataka Assembly passes bill to impose 2% cess on movie tickets and OTT |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

=== Persons with disabilities ===
During 2025, the Karnataka Labour Department worked on a proposed legislative framework for reservations for persons with disabilities in education and private-sector employment. The draft framework proposed up to 10 percent reservation in educational institutions and 5 percent in private-sector employment, subject to legislative and policy processes.<ref name="pwd">{{cite news |date=6 November 2025 |title=Karnataka plans quota for people with disabilities in education, private jobs |work=Deccan Herald}}</ref>

== Political organization ==
Lad served as General Secretary of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) and was given responsibility for Raichur district organization during his earlier period in Congress politics.

In January 2023, the Congress appointed Lad as a co-chairman in the party's Karnataka Assembly election campaign committee, with responsibility for the Belagavi division.<ref name="campaign">{{cite press release |title=Appointments to the Campaign Committee of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee |date=14 January 2023 |publisher=Indian National Congress}}</ref>

He also participated in Congress's Bharat Jodo Yatra activities in Karnataka in 2022.<ref name="bharatjodo">{{cite news |date=12 October 2022 |title=Bharat Jodo Yatra to eliminate the caste system says Santosh Lad |work=Asianet News}}</ref>

Lad started his political career as a counsellor from Sandur taluk. He had very little success in Pattana panchayat elections, where he lost marginally in his first election. He went on to win both seats he contested in the following election, contributing to his party gaining the majority during that period.

Lad contested the MLA election against a strong contender from the Congress Party. He represented the [[Janata Dal (Secular)]] party and was the youngest MLA (aged 29), along with the first person from his party to win [[Sandur, India|Sandur]] constituency; the election was won with a record margin. Lad was part of the government formation under [[H. D. Kumaraswamy]], ex-chief minister of the Karnataka state.

In the 2008 Karnataka Assembly elections, he won the Kalaghatgi constituency in the Dharwad district. He currently is an active member and represents [[Indian National Congress]]. In the 2013 Karnataka state assembly election, Santosh Lad won with a margin of over 45,000 votes,<ref>{{cite news|last=H D|first=Uttam|title=Karnataka polls: List of winners, constituency-wise results |url=http://www.indiatvnews.com/politics/national/karnataka-polls-list-of-winners-constituency-wise-results--9969.html?page=3|newspaper=India TV News|date=8 May 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=H D|first=Uttam|url=http://www.rediff.com/news/karnataka-assembly-elections-2013/dharwad/kalghatgi-75|work=Rediff.com|title=Rediff Labs: Kalghatgi Karnataka Assembly Elections 2013}}</ref> to win consecutively for the second time from Kalaghatgi and third time overall. Congress secured an absolute majority to form the government.<ref>{{cite news|last=H D|first=Uttam|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/home/specials/news/Karnataka-election-results-Congress-wins-BJP-suffers-humiliating-defeat/articleshow/19949066.cms|newspaper=The Times of India|title=Karnataka election results: Congress wins, BJP suffers humiliating defeat}}</ref> Santosh Lad was appointed Minister of State for Information and Infrastructure. In 2018, legislative elections, he lost to C.M. Nimbannanavar of the BJP, with a margin of 20,997 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minister / Officers' Details |url=http://www.iddkarnataka.gov.in/officers.html |publisher=[[Government of Karnataka]] |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609065228/http://www.iddkarnataka.gov.in/officers.html |archive-date=June 9, 2013 |language=en}}</ref>

===Initiatives===
Santosh Lad was appointed state representative to oversee the rescue operation in the worst flooded area of Uttarakhand,<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.dnaindia.com/bangalore/1851433/report-karnataka-government-scrambles-to-rescue-kannadigas-stuck-in-uttarakhand |title = Karnataka government scrambles to rescue Kannadigas stuck in Uttarakhand|date = 22 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bangalore/54-more-return-from-Uttarakhand/articleshow/20884998.cms | work=The Times of India | title=54 more return from Uttarakhand | date=3 July 2013}}</ref> accompanied by a team headed by Hemanth Nimbalkar, Kari Gowda, and Naveen Raj Singh. After over ten days of rescue operations, the team was able to rescue everyone except 14 people for whom an extensive search was carried out.

==Positions held==
*1998 – Elected councilor, Sandur Town Panchayat
*2002- Sandur Municipal Council
*2004 – Elected MLA from Sandur representing Janata Dal (Secular)
*2007 – Joined Indian National Congress
*2008 – Elected MLA from Kalaghatgi representing Indian National Congress
*2010 – Appointed general secretary of KPCC
*2010 – Appointed Raichur District in charge by KPCC
*2013 – Wins second time in a row as MLA from Kalaghatgi
*2013 – Appointed Minister of State for Information and Infrastructure
*2016- Appointed Minister of State for Labour and Skill Development
*2023 - Appointed Labour minister of Karnataka.
*2026- Appointed Labour and Employment minister of Karnataka.

==Personal life==
[[File:Shivaji Lad with Santosh Lad.jpg|thumb|310x310px|Shivaji Lad with Santosh Lad]]
Lad's father, Shivaji, died when Santosh was 16 years old. He is married to Keerthi Lad; they have a son, Karan Lad. His 2023 election affidavit identifies him as a businessman/entrepreneur and identifies his spouse's occupation as homemaker.<ref name="affidavit"/>
